title: MV Is it possible to swap leader and follower with an animation in RMMV?

posts.author: Fr4ncioh
posts.body:
Hi everyone,
I’m working on a puzzle game in RPG Maker MV with a two-character party: a Leader (ID 1) and a Follower (ID 2) (which never changes). I want to create a system where pressing a key, like G (G For "Group"), swaps the Leader and Follower with a visible, animated movement. The idea is that the current Leader steps backward while the Follower moves forward into the Leader’s position, or vice versa depending on the current swap. Before swapping, the system should record the direction the front character is facing so both characters maintain correct facing after the swap. If a character cannot move (for example, blocked by a wall or something with collision), the step animation should be skipped to prevent clipping or softlocks of any kinds.
I imagine this would work as a parallel common event running at the start of the game. The swap should keep the two characters in formation (ID's won't be swapped), one behind the other, and automatically restore the follower to follow the leader after the movement. I’m not sure if fully achieving this animation (or anything i just wrote) is possible using only vanilla MV, so if it’s not, I’m open to using a custom plugin or script to make it work (As long as it's not AI gen).
I'm kinda lost... even because i don't know if i can move followers at all, so thanks in advance for any advice or suggestions! ^_^

posts.author: coucassi
posts.body:
I think it's possible just with eventing, if you are willing to put in a bit of work. You'll have to create events with the same sprites as both actors on every map you want this to work on. Also they should have the same event IDs on every map, so that you can control them with a common event (or you have to put
this
event also on every map as a parallel process^^). With this event, activated on button press, you need to get the position and facing direction of your actors and then move the events with the corresponding sprites to the exact same location (for example with a jump command). If you make them invisible at first and just activate the event page with the sprite after they are above your actors and then make your actors invisible, nobody will notice they switched places. From here on you can just controll there movements via moveroutes. Afterwards you remove your party leader from the party and then add them again. This will make them switch positions. Now you make them visible again and turn the doppelganger events off.
If you want a specific button that is not covered by the conditions for conditional branches, you'll probably also need a plugin for button press though. And if you are going to use plugins, you can spare yourself a lot of work with just using a follower control plugin like
this one
.

◆If：Script：Input.isTriggered('g') && $gameSystem.isFormationEnabled()
◆Script：var dir = $gamePlayer.direction();
：Script：var f = $gamePlayer.followers().follower(0);
：Script：$gameParty.swapOrder(0, 1);
：Script：$gamePlayer.setDirection(dir);
：Script：if (f) f.setDirection(dir);
◆
：End

posts.author: coucassi
posts.body:
Of course I'm fine with it. If it works out for you, you can just credit me as coucassi if you want, but it's not necessary^^ Just note a few things:
- I went the eventing way, wherever possible, so if you familiar with scripting you could break down most of the steps.
- A lot of the commands are in german, because I use the maker in my native language. Knowing how the engine works, I think you'll be fine though. If anything is unclear, I'm happy to explain.
- I did not use a script to ask for the button press of G, but the default conditional branch asking for shift. You'll have to change that.
I used:
4 Switches [498 - 501]
2 Variables [170 & 171]
2 Events (You'll have to copy them to every map, where you want the leader switch to be possible)
1 Common Event
Heres my Common Event. You have to set it to
parallel
. I used
Switch #500
. You'll need it later.

Here's the two other events. You'll have to copy them to every map and make sure they always have the same ID (in this case it's 14 & 15)
Event 14
Event 15
Switch 499, which let's the Event know that your main character is the current leader is best set to ON manually at the beginning of you game.
Switch 500, which enables the common event is best manually set on as soon as you want the leader switchiung to be possible.
